18:1: Praise belongs to Allah, Who sent down the Book upon His servant and did not make any crookedness in it.
18:2: As an upright Book, to warn of a severe punishment from His presence and to give glad tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that there is a good reward for them.
18:3: They are dwellers in it forever.
18:4: And to warn those who say, "Allah has taken a child."
18:5: There is no knowledge for them concerning it, nor for their fathers. How grave is the word that comes out of their mouths! They speak nothing but a lie.
18:6: Then perhaps you, upon their footsteps, if they do not believe in this word, will destroy yourself in grief.
18:7: Indeed, We have made whatever is on the earth an adornment for it, so that We may test them, which of them is better in deed.
18:8: And indeed, We will surely make whatever is upon it dry, barren soil.
18:9: Or did you think that the people of Kehf and Rakim were a wonder among Our signs?
18:10: When the young men took refuge in the cave and said: "Our Rabb, grant us a mercy from Your presence and prepare for us a right course in our affair."
18:11: Thereupon, We struck their ears in the cave for a number of years.
18:12: Then We woke them up, so that We might know which of the two groups better calculated the duration they remained.
18:13: We narrate to you their story with truth; indeed, they are young men who believed in their Rabb, and We increased them in guidance.
18:14: And We strengthened their hearts; when they stood up, they said: "Our Rabb is the Rabb of the heavens and the earth, never shall we call upon a deity other than Him; by oath, we would then surely have spoken a false word."
18:15: This is our people, they have taken deities besides Him. If only they had brought a clear proof concerning them! Who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah?
18:16: Since you have distanced yourselves from them and what they worship besides Allah, then take refuge in the cave, so that your Rabb may spread His mercy for you and prepare an ease for you in your affair.
18:17: You see the sun, when it rises, it inclines away from their cave to the right side, and when it sets, it leaves them on the left side, while they are in an open space of the cave. This is of the signs of Allah. Whomever Allah guides, he is the guided one; and whomever He leads astray, you will never find for him a guiding protector.
18:18: You would think them awake, while they are asleep, and We turn them to the right and to the left, and their dog has outstretched its two front legs at the threshold. If you had looked upon them, you would surely have turned away from them in flight and been filled with terror from them.
18:19: And thus We raised them up so that they might question one another among themselves. One of them said: "How long have you stayed?" They said: "We have stayed a day or part of a day." They said: "Your Rabb knows better how long you have stayed. Now send one of you with this silver coin of yours to the city, and let him see which food is purer, and let him bring you provision from it. And let him be very cautious and let no one notice you."
18:20: Indeed, if they come upon you, they will stone you or return you to their religion, and then you will never succeed.
18:21: And thus We made them known, so that they might know that the promise of Allah is true and that there is no doubt about the coming of the Hour of Resurrection. When they were disputing among themselves about their affair, they said: "Build a building over them. Their Rabb knows them better." Those who prevailed over their affair said: "We will surely make a masjid over them."
18:22: They will say: "They are three, the fourth of them is their dog." And they will say: "They are five, the sixth of them is their dog"—throwing stones at the unseen. And they will say: "They are seven, the eighth of them is their dog." Say: "My Rabb knows their number better. None knows them except a very few." So do not debate concerning them except with an apparent debate, and do not ask anyone of them concerning them.
18:23: And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do it tomorrow,"
18:24: Except, "If Allah wills." And remember your Rabb when you forget, and say: "Perhaps my Rabb will guide me to a path more right than this."
18:25: They remained in their cave for three hundred years and added nine.
18:26: Say: "Allah knows better how long they remained. The unseen of the heavens and the earth belongs to Him. How well He sees and how well He hears! They have no protector besides Him, and He does not associate anyone in His judgment."
18:27: Recite what has been revealed to you from the Book of your Rabb; there is none to change His words, and you will never find any refuge besides Him.
18:28: And keep yourself patiently with those who call upon their Rabb morning and evening, desiring His Face, and do not turn your eyes away from them, desiring the adornment of the worldly life. And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance, who follows his desire, and whose affair is excess.
18:29: Say: "The truth is from your Rabb. So whoever wills, let him believe; and whoever wills, let him disbelieve." Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers a fire whose walls surround them completely. If they ask for help, they will be helped with water like molten metal that scalds the faces. How evil a drink and how evil a resting place!
18:30: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds—We do not let the reward of one who does good deeds be lost.
18:31: Those—for them are the Gardens of Eden, beneath which rivers flow; they will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and will wear green garments of fine silk and thick silk, reclining therein upon couches; how excellent a reward and how excellent a resting place!
18:32: Give them the example of two men. We made for one of them two gardens of grapevines and surrounded them both with date palms.
18:33: Both of the gardens yielded their produce and did not leave anything deficient of it, and We caused a river to gush forth between them.
18:34: And he had fruit. While speaking with his companion, he said to him: "I am greater than you in wealth and mightier in manpower."
18:35: And he entered his garden while wronging his soul. He said: "I do not think that this will ever perish."
18:36: And he said: "I do not think that the Hour will occur, and if I am brought back to my Rabb, I will surely find a better place of return than it."
18:37: His companion said to him while conversing with him: "Do you disbelieve in Him Who created you from dust, then from a drop of semen, then fashioned you as a man?"
18:38: "But He is Allah, my Rabb, and I do not associate anyone with my Rabb."
18:39: When you entered your garden, shouldn't you have said, 'Whatever Allah wills, power is only with Allah'? If you see me as less than you in wealth and children,
18:40: Perhaps my Rabb will give me better than your garden, and send upon it a calamity from the sky so that it becomes slippery soil.
18:41: Or its water becomes sunken so that you can never be able to find it.
18:42: And his fruits were encompassed, so he began to wring his hands over what he had spent on it. It had collapsed upon its trellises, and he was saying: 'I wish I had not associated anything with my Rabb.'
18:43: He had no company to help him other than Allah, and he was not of those who received help.
18:44: There, protection belongs to Allah, the Truth. He is better in reward and better in outcome.
18:45: Give them the example of the life of this world: It is like water We send down from the sky, with which the vegetation of the earth mingles, then it becomes dry stubble that the winds scatter; and Allah is capable of all things.
18:46: Wealth and sons are the adornment of the life of this world, and the enduring righteous deeds are better with your Rabb in reward and better in hope.
18:47: That day We make the mountains move and you see the earth flat, and We gather them leaving not one of them behind.
18:48: And they were presented before your Rabb in ranks. 'By oath, you have come to Us just as We created you the first time. Rather, you thought that We would not appoint a meeting time for you.'
18:49: When the book is placed, you see the criminals fearful of what is in it, and they say: 'Woe to us! What is with this book that it leaves nothing small or great, but enumerates it all!' And they found what they did present. And your Rabb wrongs no one.
18:50: And when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam,' they all prostrated except Iblis. He was of the jinn, and he departed from the command of his Rabb. Do you now take him and his offspring as allies instead of Me, while they are an enemy to you? What an evil exchange for the wrongdoers.
18:51: I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of their own souls, and I am not one to take the misleaders as helpers.
18:52: And that day He says: 'Call My partners whom you claimed!' They call them, but they do not answer them. And We place a place of destruction between them.
18:53: The criminals see the Fire and think that they will fall into it, and they find no place of escape from it.
18:54: By oath, We have varied and explained in this Quran every example for the people, and man is the most contentious of all things in dispute.
18:55: What prevented people from believing when guidance came to them and from asking forgiveness of their Rabb is only that the precedent of the ancients should come to them or that the punishment should confront them.
18:56: We send the messengers only as bringers of good tidings and warners. And those who disbelieve dispute with falsehood to refute the truth thereby. And they took My verses and that which they were warned of in mockery.
18:57: And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the verses of his Rabb and turns away from them and forgets what his hands have put forward? Indeed, We have placed coverings over their hearts lest they understand it, and heaviness in their ears. And even if you call them to guidance, they will never be guided.
18:58: Your Rabb is Oft-Forgiving, Possessor of mercy. If He were to seize them for what they earned, He would have hastened the punishment for them. But for them is an appointed promise from which they will find no refuge.
18:59: Those were the cities; We destroyed them when they committed injustice, and We appointed an appointed time for their destruction.
18:60: At that time Moses said to his young companion: 'I will not give up until I reach where the two seas meet, or until a long period of time passes.'
18:61: When the two reached the meeting place of the two seas, they forgot their fish, and the fish took its path in the sea (like a hole).
18:62: When they had just passed beyond, he said to his young companion: 'Bring us our meal; by oath, we have met with fatigue from this journey of ours.'
18:63: He said: 'Did you see, when we took refuge at the rock, I forgot the fish, and none made me forget it except Satan. He made me forget to mention it. And the fish took its way into the sea wondrously.'
18:64: He said: 'This is what we were seeking.' So they returned, following their footprints.
18:65: Thus they found a servant from among Our servants, to whom We had given mercy from Our presence and taught him knowledge from Our presence.
18:66: Moses said to him: 'May I follow you so that you may teach me from the right way which you have been taught?'
18:67: He said: 'Indeed, you will never be able to have patience with me.'
18:68: And how will you be patient over that which you have not encompassed the news of?'
18:69: He said: 'If Allah wills, you will find me patient, and I will not disobey you in any matter.'
18:70: He said: 'If you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I make a mention of it to you.'
18:71: So they set out, until when they embarked upon the ship, he made a hole in it. He said: 'Did you make a hole in it to drown its people? By oath, you have done an evil thing.'
18:72: He said: 'Did I not say to you, indeed you will never be able to have patience with me?'
18:73: He said: 'Do not rebuke me for what I forgot, and do not burden me with difficulty in my affair.'
18:74: So they set out, until when they met a young boy, he killed him. He said: 'Did you kill a pure soul without another soul in return? By oath, you have done a very evil thing.'
18:75: He said: 'Did I not say to you, indeed you will never be able to have patience with me?'
18:76: He said: 'If I ask you about anything after this, then do not keep company with me. Certainly, you have reached an excuse from my side.'
18:77: So they set out, until when they came to the people of a village, they asked its people for food, but they refused to host them. There they found a wall wanting to collapse, so he restored it. He said: 'If you had wished, you could have taken a payment for it.'
18:78: He said: 'This is the parting between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation of that which you could not have patience with.'
18:79: As for the ship, it belonged to poor people who worked on the sea, so I wanted to make it defective, because behind them was a king who seized every ship by force.
18:80: As for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared that he would overburden them with rebellion and disbelief.
18:81: So we desired that their Rabb should substitute for them one better than him, closer in purity and closer in mercy.
18:82: As for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city. Beneath it was a treasure belonging to them. Their father was a righteous man. Your Rabb willed that they should reach their age of maturity and extract their treasure as a mercy from your Rabb. And I did not do it of my own command. This is the interpretation of that which you could not endure.
18:83: They ask you about Dhul-Qarnayn. Say: 'I will recite to you a remembrance of him.'
18:84: Indeed, We established him upon the earth and gave him a way to everything.
18:86: Until, when he reached the place where the sun sets, he found it setting in a spring of dark mud, and he found a people near it. We said: 'O Dhul-Qarnayn! Either you punish or adopt goodness among them'.
18:87: He said: 'Whoever does wrong, we will punish him. Then he is returned to his Rabb, and He punishes him with a punishment to be denied.'
18:88: 'And whoever believes and does righteous deeds, for him there is a good reward. We will speak to him of ease from our affair.'
18:90: Until, when he reached the place where the sun rises, he found it rising upon a people for whom We had not made any cover other than it.
18:91: Thus it was; We had encompassed what was with him in knowledge.
18:93: Until, when he reached between the two barriers, he found beside them a people who could barely understand speech.
18:94: They said: 'O Dhul-Qarnayn, surely Gog and Magog are corrupters in the earth; shall we pay you a tribute on condition that you make a barrier between us and them?'
18:95: He said: 'That in which my Rabb has established me is better; so help me with strength, so that I may make a barrier between you and them.'
18:96: 'Bring me blocks of iron.' When he leveled between the two mountain sides, he said: 'Blow.' When he made it a fire, he said: 'Bring to me, that I may pour molten copper over it.'
18:97: Thus they were not able to scale it, nor were they able to pierce it.
18:98: He said: 'This is a mercy from my Rabb. When the promise of my Rabb comes, He will make it level. And the promise of my Rabb was true.'
18:99: And on that Day We leave them, some of them surging into others, and the Sur is blown, so We gather them all together.
18:100: And on that Day We clearly present Hell to the disbelievers.
18:101: Those whose eyes were within a veil from My remembrance and who were not able to hear.
18:102: Did those who disbelieve think that they could take My servants as protectors besides Me? Surely We have prepared Hell as a lodging for the disbelievers.
18:103: Say: 'Shall we inform you of those greatest in loss in deeds?'
18:104: They are those whose efforts have gone to waste in the worldly life, and they think that they are doing good works.
18:105: Those are the ones who disbelieved in the verses of their Rabb and meeting Him, thus their deeds have come to naught, so on the Day of Resurrection We will not assign any weight to them.
18:106: That is their recompense: Hell, because they disbelieved and took My verses and My messengers in mockery.
18:107: Surely for those who believe and do righteous deeds, the gardens of Firdaws are a lodging.
18:108: They are eternal dwellers therein; they do not desire any other place than it.
18:109: Say: 'If the sea were ink for the words of my Rabb, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Rabb were exhausted, even if We brought another like it.'
18:110: Say: 'I am only a human being like you; it is revealed to me that your god is one god. So whoever hopes to meet his Rabb, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in worship of his Rabb.'
